description: Oscillator that builds its wave from four quarters, each a curve of the form y equals x to the power n, with a switch that turns the whole thing into a one-shot envelope

params.text: Sets the pitch, -54 to +54 semitones around C4 at 261.63Hz
Sets the exponent of the first quarter of the wave, -10 to +10
Sets the exponent of the second quarter of the wave, -10 to +10
Sets the exponent of the third quarter of the wave, -10 to +10
Sets the exponent of the fourth quarter of the wave, -10 to +10
Divides the frequency, 1 for none and 128 for the lowest, on a continuous scale rather than whole steps
Down, the module runs free as an oscillator; up, it plays its shape once on each reset and then holds, and RESET becomes the trigger that starts it
Down, the wave is passed at whatever level the exponents produce; up, it is held to ±10V before the output halves it

inputs.text: Sets the pitch, 1V per octave, added to the FREQ knob
Adds to the POW1 knob, one unit of exponent per volt, and the total is not held to the knob's own range
Adds to the POW2 knob, one unit of exponent per volt, and the total is not held to the knob's own range
Adds to the POW3 knob, one unit of exponent per volt, and the total is not held to the knob's own range
Adds to the POW4 knob, one unit of exponent per volt, and the total is not held to the knob's own range
Sets the phase back to the start while the voltage here is at or above 1V; it is a level and not an edge, so a held gate pins the oscillator at the start of its cycle

outputs.text: The wave, or the envelope when ENV is up, at half the internal level, so ±5V with CLIP up

notes: The four POW jacks are read as single voltages, so one polyphonic cable into V/OCT gives every channel the same four exponents.
The small green drawing at the top shows the shape the four exponents make, redrawn as they are turned.
